name: Masseter reduction surgery

card.summary: Surgical thinning or removal of part of the chewing muscle to slim a wide or square lower face.
card.note: Irreversible surgery; botulinum toxin and bone contouring are alternatives discussed in the literature.

quick.overview:
The masseter is the thick chewing muscle at the angle of the jaw. When large, from clenching, grinding or heavy chewing, or when the underlying bone angle is prominent, it widens the lower face. Masseter reduction surgery removes or thins part of it to give a slimmer, more tapered jaw line.

Surgery is one of several routes; others are botulinum toxin injections that shrink the muscle and bone-contouring procedures on the mandibular angle. Published work includes clinical reports and animal studies on growth effects.
quick.how: The procedure is done by surgeons, usually in Asia-focused aesthetic practice, and can be combined with mandibular angle reduction. Recovery and results depend on the surgeon and approach, which is a clinical matter.
quick.risks: Surgical risks include bleeding and nerve injury (noted for related masticatory muscle surgery). Rat studies show masseter resection during growth reduced jaw development, so research on it in growing individuals is cautionary.

lead: Masseter reduction surgery, also called masseter resection, surgically thins the masseter, the main jaw-closing muscle, to slim the lower face. The masseter raises the lower jaw and can enlarge with clenching, grinding or frequent chewing [1].

The appearance goal is a narrower, smoother jawline, particularly where a wide lower face stems from muscle thickness. A plastic surgery paper notes the lower third of the face tends to be wider in Asian faces and is determined by the mandibular bone, muscle and fat, and that surgical muscle resection and angle ostectomy are the surgical approaches, with botulinum toxin proposed as a nonsurgical alternative [2].
Related work includes reduction gonioplasty, which cuts the jaw angle without touching the masseter; at four-year follow-up, patients' masseters had shrunk by about 21 percent [3].

chain: Part of masseter removed or thinned
angle.text: Removing bulk from an enlarged masseter reduces lower-face width. It is one of several options with botulinum toxin and bone contouring.

paras: The masseter has three heads, is supplied by the trigeminal nerve and its enlargement is usually painless and often bilateral [1].

A 2005 report described 1,021 patients treated with botulinum toxin type A (Dysport) for lower facial contouring, with ultrasound measuring muscle thickness change in 383 followed at least three months [2]. A retrospective study of reduction gonioplasty found masseter volume fell by 21 percent over four years and all patients were satisfied [3].

A systematic review of seven rat studies found masseter resection significantly reduced sagittal and vertical jaw development and altered mandibular shape [4]. Resection in young rats also affected temporomandibular joint responses to forced jaw opening [5][6]. Surgery for masticatory muscle tendon-aponeurosis hyperplasia carries bleeding and nerve damage risk, prompting use of an ultrasonic bone scalpel [7].
Human data are mostly case series: botulinum toxin contouring [2] and masseter changes after gonioplasty [3]. Resection-specific work is largely animal research [4][5][6].

timeline.event: Botulinum toxin for mandibular contouring described as alternative to surgery [2].
Long-term masseter changes after gonioplasty reported [3].
